name: wavelet_decomposition_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Financial price series contain information at multiple time scales — noise at the shortest scales, intraday trends at medium scales, and session-level direction at longer scales. Wavelet decomposition (Daubechies db4, 3-level) separates these scales cleanly, unlike moving averages which blur all frequencies together. By reconstructing the price using only the level-2 and level-3 detail coefficients (capturing 4-bar to 16-bar cycles), we extract the 'tradeable frequency' while discarding both noise (level-1) and slow drift (approximation). Trading signals are generated from the denoised price crossover with the original price. The inefficiency exists because wavelet analysis requires signal processing knowledge foreign to most traders.
mechanism: Institutional order flow arrives in bursts via algorithmic execution (TWAP/VWAP slicing), creating persistent directional pressure over 30-120 seconds. Retail and smaller participants follow the initial move, extending momentum before liquidity absorbs the flow and the order book rebalances.

conditions: close crosses above Wavelet_Denoised (raw price emerging above denoised trend)
Detail_Energy_L2 > 0.20 (sufficient energy at tradeable frequency — market is moving)

exit.signal_exit: Denoised_Slope crosses zero against position direction

weaknesses: Wavelet decomposition on a rolling window introduces boundary effects — the most recent coefficients are least reliable, which is precisely where trading signals are generated
The 64-bar minimum window means no trading until 10:20 IST, missing the morning session; and each recomputation on the full window adds latency

Choosing db4 wavelet and 3-level decomposition is somewhat arbitrary — different wavelets (Haar, Symlet) and levels produce different decompositions, and there's no principled way to select the 'right' one for financial data
prior_art: Ramsey & Lampart (1998) on wavelets in economics; Gençay et al. (2001) 'An Introduction to Wavelets and Other Filtering Methods in Finance and Economics'; wavelet denoising for trading signals in Addison (2002)
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
